## 13. Records: evidence of what ran

From [docs/pages/13-records-evidence-of-what-ran.md](../../../../docs/pages/13-records-evidence-of-what-ran.md). The read-only collection recipe: pagination, attempts and what you couldn't read.

### Collecting from the API without losing runs

Any baseline, audit or report you build from the provider's API (Phase 2) follows the completeness and estimator contract in [`skills/ci-doctor/references/speed-up-tests/references/ci-history-data.md`](../speed-up-tests/references/ci-history-data.md). In short: split search windows below the API's caps and page every list; keep every attempt; join runs to PRs by explicit relations, not branch names; keep main's and release costs apart; name the quantile estimator and the timestamps used; pair deploys by build identity; and count what you didn't read. An unread outcome is never a zero wait, a zero cost or a success.

A read-only baseline on GitHub Actions, run with the access you already have, into a scratch folder:

```sh
gh auth status                                  # who you are; ask for a missing scope, never a token
gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.core          # keep a reserve for other work
# Runs of each workflow in the current gate, in a closed UTC window. A query returns at most
# 1,000 runs: if total_count reaches it, split the window and query again.
gh api --paginate "repos/$slug/actions/workflows/$workflow/runs?event=pull_request&created=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z..2026-11-14T23:59:59Z&per_page=100" \
  --jq '.workflow_runs[] | [.id, .run_attempt, .head_sha, .status, .conclusion, .created_at, .run_started_at, .updated_at] | @tsv'
# Every attempt of each run, and its jobs and steps (queue, start, end and conclusion).
gh api "repos/$slug/actions/runs/$run/attempts/$attempt"
gh api --paginate "repos/$slug/actions/runs/$run/attempts/$attempt/jobs?per_page=100"
# PRs, paged on their own: those with no runs count too. Each PR's timeline says when it was ready.
gh api --paginate "repos/$slug/pulls?state=all&per_page=100"
gh api --paginate "repos/$slug/issues/$pr/timeline?per_page=100"
```

Repeat the run query without `event=` for spend, which counts pushes, schedules and dispatches too. Note partial reruns, expired logs and anything you were denied, with how much it covers. If the user's access can't read something, ask for that exact permission or an export they redact; don't widen tokens or archive unfiltered logs. Sources: GitHub's [workflow runs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs) and [workflow jobs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs) APIs.

## Records: evidence of what ran

From [scripts/records/README.md](../../../../scripts/records/README.md). Per-file timings: what Vitest needs, and what pytest already writes.

### 1. The reporter

Set this up only once the user approves the plan ([ci-doctor, "Before approval"](../../SKILL.md#before-approval-read-only)). Adding records changes nothing about what the gate accepts: keep the repo's current failure and retry behaviour in the same change.

In your Vitest config, add the reporter when CI asks for records. Vitest times every import anyway; the limit only says how many it reports per file, one more than the record keeps because the file itself is among them.

```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

const ciRecord = process.env.CI_RECORD === '1';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // 0 unless the user approved the in-process retry as its own change: with 1, a test that fails
    // then passes doesn't turn the run red, and is recorded as flaky (../flakes/).
    retry: Number(process.env.TEST_RETRY ?? 0),
    ...(ciRecord
      ? {
          reporters: ['default', 'github-actions', './scripts/records/test-record.ts'],
          experimental: { importDurations: { limit: 6 } },
        }
      : {}),
  },
});
```

A job that doesn't use the config's reporters can pass `--reporter=default --reporter=./scripts/records/test-record.ts`.

### Python tests

The reporter and collector here are Vitest's. For pytest, use the runner you have and its own reports:

- **Cases:** if CI already writes JUnit XML, read that. Otherwise propose `--junitxml=<file>` ([pytest's JUnit XML](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/output.html#creating-junitxml-format-files)). Its `time` per case includes setup and teardown by default (`junit_duration_report`).
- **Phases:** `--durations=0` prints every setup, call and teardown time ([profiling durations](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/usage.html#profiling-test-execution-duration)), so you can see a session fixture's cost.
- **These are durations, not file wall time.** Case times, session fixtures, collection and concurrent workers (`pytest-xdist`) don't sum to how long a file took. For shard balancing, time collection and each file's, or each worker lane's, elapsed time around the command itself.
- **Each observation carries** suite, path and environment, plus the SHA, run attempt, shard, skip, failure and retry status, and whether it ran or was replayed from a cache.
- **Keep them small:** a structured log line like `ci-record`'s, or a small artifact, once the user approves it.
- **Keep Python and TypeScript timings apart** unless they were measured on the same basis.
